reading.body:
DartPoints Baton Rouge 2 publishes 3 MW of IT capacity. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 3 MW supports roughly 75 racks; at 10 kW per rack, a more typical enterprise density, it supports roughly 300 racks. Those are assumptions about rack density, not operator claims. No redundancy tier, power usage effectiveness figure, or cooling architecture is published, so no further inference about uptime class or thermal headroom is warranted.

Certifications are not published in the specification data provided, so no statement about what compliance regimes this campus satisfies can be made.

Within Louisiana, this site ranks first by published IT capacity, but that ranking reflects a data gap rather than dominance: only 1 of the 4 mapped facilities in the state publishes a megawatt figure, and that facility is this one. The state total of published capacity is therefore exactly 3 MW, the entirety of which belongs to this campus. Three megawatts is a small footprint by the standards of campuses built to serve large-scale AI training, which routinely run into tens or hundreds of megawatts. Whether this site is relevant to AI workloads depends on use cases, such as inference at the edge or regional network aggregation, that do not require dense GPU clusters, but that determination requires tenant and workload data that is not published.
